sections.html:
Dover is the county seat of Strafford County and the most populous city in the Seacoast region, with 34,623 residents, fifth among New Hampshire cities. The Piscataqua River forms its eastern edge and the state line with Maine. The city covers 29.04 square miles, of which 26.73 are land, and most addresses sit in the Dover School District, which has about 4,000 pupils.

Dover claims the oldest permanent settlement in New Hampshire, begun in 1623 at Dover Point, and it became a city in 1855. Textile mills along Cochecho Falls built the downtown, and that left a stock of older homes close to the center. Houses of that age often carry original wiring, old plumbing or additions built without paperwork, and those are the items a buyer's inspector tends to raise.

The old mill complex has found new uses. Cocheco Falls Millworks now holds technology and government services companies, and the Children's Museum of New Hampshire occupies a former mill. Wentworth-Douglass Hospital is based in the city.

sections.h2: Getting in and out of Dover
sections.html:
Commuting access is one of the first things a Dover buyer asks about. The routes are NH 4, 9, 16 (the Spaulding Turnpike), 108 and 155, plus U.S. Route 4. Transit is broader than in many New Hampshire cities of this size:

  • Amtrak's Downeaster stops at the Dover Transportation Center, with service to Portland, Maine, and Boston North Station
  • C&J Bus Lines runs intercity service to Boston South Station, Logan Airport and the New York Port Authority
  • COAST operates a publicly funded bus network in New Hampshire and Maine
  • Wildcat Transit serves Durham, free for UNH students and $1.50 for the public

A house within reach of the train or the Spaulding Turnpike draws a different pool of buyers than one that is not, so mention the commute options when you describe your property.

sections.h2: Property tax rate and due dates
sections.html:
Dover's 2025 tax rate is $19.68 per $1,000 of assessed value, certified by the New Hampshire Department of Revenue Administration. It has four parts.

Tax year 2025 rate components
Part of the rateRate per $1,000
City6.91
County1.83
State school1.16
City school9.78
Total19.68

Bills are mailed twice a year. The first half is due December 1 and the second half June 1, and interest accrues at 12% a year after a due date. Exact dates can shift because the state sets the rate, so call the City Clerk and Tax Collector at 603-516-6018 before you rely on a date.

sections.h2: Your assessment and how to appeal it
sections.html:
Dover did not run its annual citywide revaluation for tax year 2025. The assessment office judged that current values still met assessing standards, and skipping the update made for a cleaner move to a new computer-assisted mass appraisal system. The city mailed value change notices to 993 properties instead. The assessor estimated a 5% market increase for the year, and leaving values alone kept an equalization ratio of 89% to 90%. By state law, values reflect conditions on April 1, the first day of the tax year.

If you think your assessment is wrong, file an abatement application with the Tax Assessment Office by March 1 of the following year. Filing does not stop collection, so pay as billed. If the city denies the application or does not act by July 1, you can appeal by September 1 to the Board of Tax and Land Appeals or to superior court, not both. The assessment office is at 603-516-6014.

Unpaid Dover taxes can end in a lien and, eventually, a deed to the city. Certified notices go out in July, and liens are recorded at the Registry of Deeds in August, with interest at 18% a year on the lien amount from the lien date.

A lien can be redeemed within two years by paying everything owed plus interest and fees. A property with an unredeemed lien can be deeded to the city at least two years and one day after the lien date. A sale is one way to clear a balance before a lien forms, and a cash buyer does not need a lender to review the arrears.

If you are behind, call the Tax Collector and ask for a written payoff with interest calculated to a named day. Hand that letter to your closing agent so the balance is paid from your proceeds.

Dover Inspection Services handles building permits from 269 Mast Road, next to the public works complex, and applications go through the city's online permit portal. The office can be reached at 603-516-6038.

The state codes in effect when a permit is applied for stay in force for that work, and Dover may adopt stricter building and fire codes by ordinance. If a previous owner finished a basement or added a deck, check that a permit exists before you list. Missing paperwork tends to surface during a buyer's inspection and can slow a financed sale. A cash buyer will still ask about it, but the conversation is usually simpler.

New Hampshire's transfer tax is $.75 per $100 of the price, charged to each of the buyer and the seller under RSA 78-B and filed through the Granite Tax Connect portal. Your closing agent will show the exact amount on the settlement statement.

Sellers of one to four family homes must also give written disclosures on private water and sewage, insulation, flood hazard zone and any underground heating oil tank under RSA 477:4-d. Fill the form out early, because an incomplete one can hold up the contract.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works in Dover
sections.html:
In a cash sale you describe the Dover house, receive an offer and choose whether to accept, with no obligation if you say no. There is no lender appraisal, so the repairs a financed buyer might demand do not hold up the closing.

The steps that stay the same are the title search, the tax proration and the state's transfer tax and disclosure rules. Before you agree to a closing date, get your tax payoff, locate your permits and decide what you want to leave in the house. That short list keeps the timeline tight and avoids surprises at the table.

faqs.q: What is Dover's property tax rate?
faqs.a: The 2025 rate is $19.68 per $1,000 of assessed value, made up of 6.91 city, 1.83 county, 1.16 state school and 9.78 city school.

faqs.q: When are Dover property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first half is due December 1 and the second half June 1. Call the City Clerk and Tax Collector at 603-516-6018 to confirm a date.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Dover assessment?
faqs.a: File an abatement application with the Tax Assessment Office by March 1 following the tax bill. If the city denies it or does not act by July 1, you can appeal by September 1 to the Board of Tax and Land Appeals or superior court, not both.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell a house in Dover?
faqs.a: Yes. New Hampshire charges $.75 per $100 of the price to each of the buyer and the seller under RSA 78-B, filed through the Granite Tax Connect portal.

faqs.q: Does Dover have train service for commuters?
faqs.a: Yes. Amtrak's Downeaster stops at the Dover Transportation Center, with service to Portland, Maine, and Boston North Station.
